A study has designed a system based on fiber Bragg grating sensing technology to measure the deformation of piezoelectric composite resonators under temperature variations. Using this system, three-dimensional deformations of various composite materials were measured from 25°C to 120°C, confirming the feasibility of the system and providing a practical testing approach to identify piezoelectric composite resonators with superior heat resistance.

articleTitle: Study of the sensitivity mechanism of a flexible temperature sensor
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a structure of a flexible temperature sensor is proposed. And its sensitivity mechanism is investigated. A physical model is established based on the proposed structure. A mathematical model is established based on the actual situation. A 3D model of the structure is created by COMSOL software. In which the mathematical model is studied for this sensor. The temperature field within this sensitive structure was calculated using the finite element method. The corresponding material properties in the sensor structure were set. Setting up the physical fields required for operation. Mesh this 3D structure. Setting the external ambient temperature. Setup of the type of study according to the actual situation. The sensor detects the ambient temperature. Calculations are made based on the results of the finite element method, combined with the corresponding theoretical formulas. It is calculated that the temperature coefficient of resistance is 0.0316/° C in the temperature range of -18~80 ° C, and the nonlinearity is 1.36%. There results conclude that the relationship between temperature and resistance is proportional. This lays a theoretical foundation for the optimisation of subsequent structural studies of flexible temperature sensors. It facilitates further performance enhancement in subsequent research. This promotes the research progress in related fields.

articleTitle: Wind speed forecasting in high-speed railway system based on secondary decomposition and gated recurrent unit network
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Accurately predicting wind speed (WS) is crucial for the operational safety of high-speed railway (HSR) systems in strong wind environments. However, the prediction task is challenging due to WS data's nonlinearity and intermittency nature. To address this issue, this study proposes a hybrid prediction model SD-BGRU, which combines secondary decomposition (SD), sample entropy (SE), and gated recurrent unit (GRU). Specifically, the raw WS signal is first decomposed using complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition adaptive noise (CEEMDAN). The decomposed data are clustered into three groups based on their SE. VMD is then applied to further decompose sub-signals with high SE values. The remaining sub-signals obtained from CEEMDAN and sub-signals obtained from VMD are fed into bidirectional GRU (BGRU) to generate individual predictions. These prediction results are combined to produce a final prediction result. We conducted extensive experiments on a real-world WS dataset to evaluate the performance of SD-BGRU. The experiment results demonstrate that SD-BGRU outperforms other comparative models, with a mean absolute error of 0.3395, root mean square error of 0.4571, and mean absolute percentage error of 8.88%. These promising results indicate that SD-BGRU is an effective way for guiding decision-making in the HSR system.

articleTitle: Research on false alarm and diagnosis methods of signal alarm system in nuclear power plant
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The signal alarm systems of nuclear power plants play an important role for the safety of operation. If the signal alarm system itself fails or malfunctions, the faults or abnormal situations of the main systems and equipment of the nuclear power plant may be masked, causing operators to have illusions and take incorrect decisions or operational actions, increasing the safety risks of nuclear power plant operation. To assist operators in understanding the mechanism of false alarms in the alarm system, the fault tree method was used to analyse the false alarm mechanism of the nuclear power plant alarm system. Based on the composition of the alarm system, fault trees for false alarms and reject alarms in the signal alarm system were established. Through fault tree analysis, obtain the fault discrimination rules for false alarms in the alarm system. On this basis, a false alarm diagnosis method for signal alarm systems based on fault tree analysis and inference fusion was studied, and the diagnostic process was provided with examples.

articleTitle: A fibre-optic high-speed lighting spectrograph
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Natural lightning is random and transient, and precise research on the internal characteristics of lightning discharge channels requires high-resolution measurements. And the existing regenerative spectrometers have low time resolution, so it is particularly important to design a fibre-optic lightning high-speed spectrometer device with high time resolution. The article introduces a fibre-optic high-speed lightning spectrometer device, i.e. using the grating diffraction principle to decompose lightning into spectra consisting of different wavelengths, fixing the position of the bright stripe in the centre of the lightning spectrum with a spectral positioning camera, picking up the light intensity signals with N fibre-optic arrays uniformly arranged on the spectral lines of different wavelengths and transmitting the light signals to a high-speed data acquisition module, which will perform the data acquisition after photoelectric conversion. It involves the fields of optics and electricity. The device includes: a grating, a convex lens, a receiving screen, a fibre optic, a photoelectric converter, a high speed data acquisition module and a spectral positioning camera. The device can measure the high time resolution waveform variation curves of N light components of different wavelengths or frequencies of a lighting, which can be used for more detailed lighting studies.

articleTitle: MCGAN: a novel channel estimation method for load management systems
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Precise channel estimation is fundamental to ensuring the reliability, response time, and data accuracy in load management systems, particularly in complex power system environments where communication issues arise from multipath fading and propagation interference. This paper presents an innovative channel estimation method specifically designed for load management systems. The proposed method employs a Channel Generative Adversarial Network (Channel GAN) architecture, combining Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (SRGAN) and Denoising Generative Adversarial Network (DnGAN) techniques. This approach is further enhanced by a Multi-Layer Attention Mechanism (MLAM) to focus on pertinent features and improve the robustness of the model. The Channel GAN competes between a generator and discriminator, facilitating the learning of robust feature representations for effective reconstruction and denoising in Frequency-Bell Multicarrier (FBMC) communication systems. Moreover, the MLAM and multi-modal fusion strategies allow for more precise channel parameter estimation by concentrating resources on essential feature extraction. This method, grounded in deep learning techniques, successfully addresses the challenges of high complexity and low estimation accuracy in FBMC systems. Experimental evaluations confirm that the proposed scheme surpasses traditional methods in terms of accuracy and adaptability. This work contributes to the ongoing efforts in enhancing the operation and maintenance of load management systems within smart grid infrastructures.

articleTitle: Measurement system construction of transient waveform signal source
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The power source of the distribution automation terminal detection platform is one of the important devices for simulating the fault signal of the distribution network and testing the performance of the distribution safety equipment. The power source is programmable, and a fault signal is written to it, and the power source can be used to simulate the corresponding fault signal, which is of short duration, usually a transient signal. In this paper, a measurement system based on the transient signal of the analog output of the power source is constructed, and the quality of the measured signal waveform is evaluated. In this paper, the transient signal is divided into transient voltage signal and transient current signal, and the voltage and current are repeatedly measured by two measurement systems. The maximum offset of the signal amplitude and the maximum offset of the phase are used to evaluate the difference between the measured transient signal and the transient signal waveform written to the power source, and to evaluate whether the performance of the power source is intact. The amplitude and phase maximum offset obtained by the experimental data are small, showing a high uniformity, and it can be concluded that the power source used in this paper has good performance and can accurately simulate the output fault signal.

articleTitle: Research progress on fault diagnosis of mining gearbox based on CiteSpace
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Mining gearboxes are mechanical devices used to reduce rotational speed and increase torque, widely utilized in mining and heavy industrial equipment. To further understand the research progress and development trends in the field of fault diagnosis for mining gearboxes, a clustering and visualization analysis of English literature was conducted using the Web of Science database and the CiteSpace method. The analysis revealed that the performance and reliability of gearboxes have consistently been focal points for researchers, with a significant community of authors contributing to this field. The co-occurrence and clustering of keywords indicated that the research content is concentrated on fault diagnosis and optimization design. Moreover, the field is evolving towards intelligent diagnostics. Future development trends should focus on the introduction of data-driven and knowledge-guided artificial intelligence algorithm models and explainable intelligent diagnostic technologies.

articleTitle: Simulation and experimental study of low-energy fluorescence X-rays
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Fluorescence X-rays have the advantages of good monochromaticity, high flux and stable dose rate. Carried out simulation and experimental studies of fluorescence X-rays in the (4.5 ~ 25.3) KeV energy range. The energy spectra produced by different radiators were simulated using Monte Carlo simulation software to obtain the theoretical spectra. The K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">β</sub>and L fluorescence X-rays were also filtered in the simulation by choosing different materials of secondary filter materials for each radiator. Measurement experiments were carried out using a HPGe detector to obtain experimental spectra. The simulation results match the experimental results, verifying the correctness of the experimental measurements. The fluorescence yield and<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Kα</sub>fluorescence purity of the radiator were calculated, in which the fluorescence yield of Zn reached percent 95.2 and the purity of K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</sub>fluorescence of Cd reached percent 82.8. The factors affecting the fluorescence yield experiment are the secondary filter corresponding to the radiator, which can be subsequently optimized in the selection of secondary filter.

articleTitle: A method for generating a synthetic dataset of armored targets: randomized scene synthesis training
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel methodology, Randomized Scene Synthesis Training (RSST), for generating synthetic datasets of armored targets to train deep neural networks effectively. RSST extends domain randomization techniques to address the challenges of collecting and annotating real-world armored vehicle data, which is often constrained by security and resource limitations. The method involves creating non-photorealistic armored target data within a graphics engine, enabling the rapid generation of large, accurately labeled datasets at a lower cost. Experiments show that a deep learning model trained on this synthetic dataset performs well in detecting armored targets in real-world images, achieving a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.692. By leveraging synthetic data, the quality and diversity of object detection datasets can be significantly improved, leading to enhanced robustness and generalization capabilities. This approach not only facilitates the training of highly accurate models but also opens new possibilities for computer vision research, particularly in overcoming the limitations of real-world data collection.

articleTitle: A study of the characteristics of the influence of the precession factor of an all-metal micro-hemispherical resonator
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The precession factor of resonant gyro is the key performance index of gyro sensitive angular velocity, and the main factors affecting the precession factor are the structural parameters of the resonator. In this paper, an all-metal micro-hemispherical resonator with a radius of 3mm is taken as the research object, the expression of the precession factor of the hemispherical resonator is established, and the intrinsic frequencies under different modal orders are obtained through the finite element simulation experimental method, and the influences of the radius of the hemispherical shell, the thickness of the shell, the diameter of the central axis rod, and the radius of the inner fillet angle on the precession factor of the resonator are analyzed. The experimental results show that the size of the inner fillet radius has a significant effect on the precession factor, and the precession factor of the metallic micro-hemispherical resonator is mainly maintained at 0.2980 with a variation range of less than 1%. This study provides reference data for the optimization of the structural parameters of the all-metal micro-hemispherical resonator.

articleTitle: Features extraction of complex dynamic electricity signals for testing dynamic errors in electricity meters
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The paper addresses the issue of rapid amplitude changes in complex dynamic electricity (CDE) signals, which can induce substantial errors in electricity metering. Firstly, a discrete signal mathematical model is established for three types of typical dynamic loads within the power grid. Secondly, six important sensitive feature parameters are identified, along with their corresponding algorithms. Subsequently, six typical run waveform modes are extracted from the amplitude domain of current run waveforms using a combination of full traversal and Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Based on these waveform modes, a library for current feature waveforms is constructed. Finally, suggestions are provided for supplementing international electricity meter standards to address the insufficiency of test points for evaluating the dynamic errors of electricity meters.

articleTitle: A software error compensation method for equivalent-time sampling oscilloscopes
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: When an equivalent sampling oscilloscope measures signals, it will inevitably introduce noise and jitter, affecting the accuracy of the signals. The traditional processing method is to design an excellent circuit to reduce the generation of errors, which is relatively complex. This paper proposes a software method based on the orthogonal distance regression algorithm to compensate for the generated errors. Compared to error compensation implemented through hardware circuits, the implementation via software algorithms is significantly more convenient. Moreover, the signal error post software compensation is substantially reduced, achieving precision at the fs scale. At the same time, by studying the orthogonal distance regression (ODR) algorithm in comparison with the ordinary least squares (OLS) method and the moving least squares (MLS) method, it was concluded that the ODR algorithm exhibits the best performance, with a relative error of less than 0.01. By optimizing the ODR algorithm from nonlinear to linear, the computation was significantly reduced. The underlying causes of significant parameter errors in the algorithm were systematically analysed to offer insights and guidance on its applicability.

articleTitle: Fatigue damage evolution analysis of drive shaft considering residual stress and hardness gradient
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The service environment of the transmission shaft is complex, and it is frequently subjected to impact load. Impact fatigue is the main cause of its fatigue failure. In this study, a fatigue damage evolution analysis method of transmission shaft considering residual stress and hardness gradient is proposed under the framework of damage irreversible thermodynamics. Firstly, combined with the wave theory, the wave effect of impact stress wave is analyzed, the evolution equation of stress wave fluctuation behavior is established, and the evolution law of stress and strain field under the action of stress wave is analyzed. Then, based on the irreversible thermodynamic framework of damage, the thermodynamic state potential and dissipation potential of the damage process are studied, and the coupling characteristics of the damage evolution dynamic response and the intrinsic damage dissipation of the damaged material are analyzed. The damage evolution model of fatigue performance degradation considering residual stress and hardness gradient is established to identify the critical condition of intrinsic damage dissipation and describe the fatigue damage failure behavior. Finally, the cohesive element of the coupled damage constitutive is defined to simulate the damage evolution behavior of the substructure, and the influence of residual stress and hardness gradient on the damage evolution is explored. The results show that different initial crack forms have an important influence on the stress wave propagation behavior. The existence of residual tensile stress accelerates the process of fatigue damage accumulation, and the improvement of surface hardness can improve the fatigue resistance of the body.

articleTitle: The design of IMB bus data processing software
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: This paper introduces Intermodule Data Bus (IMB)which is used for the C919 Flight Control System. It is necessary to develop IMB bus data processing software to provide data basis for civil aircraft airworthiness certification test flight.IMB data are collected and recorded in INET-X protocol in test system, and its bus packet data are mixed with data from other systems on the aircraft.This way of storing multi-source network data poses a problem for efficiently identifying the IMB packets in the massive INET-X data file.The paper finds that STREAMID is the key data which can uniquely identify the IMB packet from the INET-X network data and LABEL of the message block which can ultimately locate the specific parameters of the IMB bus data by analyzing the INET-X network packet format, IMB bus packet format and network packet storage features.The paper designs a set of ICD management database suitable for data analysis and studies general flow of data processing.The algorithm of time-searching based on memory mapping is used to location of IMB data in Ethernet data packet.The paper also detailed introduces of the IMB packet localization algorithm. IMB data processing software is designed with these algorithms. It has high efficiency to meet the demand of IMB bus data processing in flight test after software test.

articleTitle: Performance measurement and analysis of openable core current transformer
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The openable core current transformer is widely used in the on-site measurement due to its convenience. However, the existence of air gap leads to the decrease of core magnetic performance, so it is rarely used in the field of precision measurement. Two kinds of high quality soft magnetic materials are selected to analyse the difference of key magnetic properties before and after core cutting, so as to promote the rational configuration of materials. Establish the mathematical model for the openable core current transformer and decompose the impact of ratio error and phase displacement. Employ permalloy as the measuring core; produce a prototype of openable core current transformer; and the fractional turn error compensation is adopted. The results show that the ratio error and phase displacement of the prototype satisfy the requirement of 0.1 S class error limit, which may provide the reference for the development of high precision openable core current transformer.

articleTitle: Research on the mechanism of a high robustness pressure sensor based on heat conduction
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a structure of high robustness pressure sensor based on heat conduction is proposed and its mechanism is studied. The temperature field in the structure of a high robustness pressure transducer based on heat conduction is calculated by COMSOL, and the temperature difference under the corresponding pressure is calculated. The calculation results based on the three-dimensional physical model of the sensor show that the temperature difference of the highly robust pressure sensor based on heat conduction decreases with the increase of pressure, and the pressure of the sensor is inversely proportional to the temperature difference, The temperature sensitivity of the high robustness pressure sensor based on heat conduction in the range of 0 ~ 49N is -0.021 K/N and the nonlinearity is 11.02%. The temperature sensitivity of the high robustness pressure sensor based on heat conduction in the range of 50 ~ 60N is -1.184 K/N and the nonlinearity is 7.85%. Through the establishment of the three-dimensional physical model structure of the high-robustness pressure sensor based on heat conduction and the calculation results of the sensor, the mechanism of the high-robustness pressure sensor based on heat conduction is revealed, which lays a theoretical foundation for the subsequent optimization of the parameters and structure of this kind of sensor.

articleTitle: A scientific method for compiling the load spectrum of transmission shaft for hybrid special vehicle based on parameter extrapolation
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: To compile the load spectrum for the transmission shaft in hybrid special vehicles with high reliability, this paper employs the parameter extrapolation method for load spectrum compilation. By collecting experimental real vehicle torque load data and related driving records, the operation process of the special vehicle would be divided into 5 typical operating conditions. Throughout the pre-processed load data, the rainflow counting method is applied to develop statistically analysis and distribution-fitting. Based on the probability statistical distribution results, it could indicate that: the amplitude values for each operating condition follow a lognormal distribution; the means value for each operating condition follow a 3-parameter lognormal distribution, and they are mutually independent. Accordingly, the load extremes and frequencies are extrapolated for the target life cycle, and the rationality of the extrapolation is verified. Based on the extrapolation results, an 8-level two-dimensional load spectrum and a one-dimensional program spectrum are compiled. In general, the research results provide a foundation for the reliability testing of hybrid special vehicles.

articleTitle: Research on flight path measurement method based on monocular photography and inertial data fusion
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In accordance with ICAO DOC 9501 Volume I, external noise certification flight tests typically employ a DGPS tracking system to measure aircraft trajectory data, with regulatory requirements for verifying the accuracy of the DGPS system. This paper proposes a method for aircraft trajectory measurement based on Monocular photography, investigates the Monocular photography measurement model and the unified coordinate system algorithm, and demonstrates the feasibility of using aircraft inertial navigation data to correct the three-dimensional position of the aircraft. The method was applied in actual flight tests to measure the trajectories of the aircraft at four different altitudes and compare the data. The results show that the deviation between Monocular photography-based aircraft trajectory measurement and DGPS system data is less than 1.5 meters. This verifies the accuracy of the DGPS tracking system as required by the regulations, providing significant evidence for the application of Monocular photography measurement technology in external noise testing.

articleTitle: SOC estimation design of lithium battery based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of existing methods for estimating state of charge (SOC) of lithium battery, a novel SOC estimation scheme based on Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) with high parallelism was proposed in this paper. The second-order RC circuit is selected to be equivalent to the battery model, and the variable forgetting factor recursive least square (VFFRLS) and extended Kalman filter (EKF) algorithm is used to identify the parameters online and estimate the SOC of the lithium battery. The EKF algorithm flow is re-planned according to the high parallelism of FPGA, so that some algorithms can run in parallel, which greatly reduces the algorithm operation time and improves the SOC estimation efficiency. The modularization design idea is used to design the Verilog program structure in FPGA. The finite state machine is used to control the logical sequence between each step, so that each module runs in order and reduces the logical complexity. The pulsating integral matrix multiplier is packaged and modified, so that a single pulsating integral matrix multiplier can deal with different dimensional matrix schemes, thus reducing FPGA resource consumption. The time series simulation and experimental verification show that this scheme has high real-time performance and accuracy in estimating SOC of lithium battery.

articleTitle: Traversability estimation based on vehicle characteristics and environmental geometry
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In unstructured environments, ensuring the safe operation of autonomous vehicles necessitates precise perception and thorough analysis of the surrounding terrain. Existing traversability analysis methods frequently rely on data from a single sensor and fail to integrate vehicle characteristics with environmental geometric features. This limitation results in weak environmental perception and poor performance in traversability analysis. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an innovative approach. By fusing data from multiple LiDAR sensors, the method constructs a locally dense traversability map, significantly enhancing the completeness and reliability of terrain information.Moreover, this approach combines vehicle characteristics with multiple environmental geometric factors to generate a traversability layer. This integration leads to a more holistic understanding of the terrain, improving the vehicle's ability to navigate complex environments safely. The proposed method demonstrates outstanding performance in traversability estimation, enabling a more accurate evaluation of traversability. This, in turn, provides a solid guarantee for the safe driving of autonomous vehicles in various challenging scenarios.The system underwent rigorous testing in unstructured environments to validate its effectiveness. The test results indicate that the elevation maps and traversability layer generated by this method exhibit significant improvements in both detail and accuracy. These advancements ensure that autonomous vehicles can better perceive and navigate their surroundings, ultimately contributing to safer and more reliable autonomous driving in unstructured and complex terrains.

articleTitle: Valve positioner control based on SHO-PID controller
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: As an important accessory and control core of pneumatic regulating valves, intelligent positioners play a crucial role in industrial process control. Aiming at the requirements of steady and accurate control of intelligent valve positioners and the low efficiency of PID parameter tuning, a scheme using selfish herd optimization algorithm to optimize intelligent valve positioners is proposed. Based on the physical characteristics of the pneumatic valve system, a system model was built using Simulink. A objective function was designed based on practical requirements to enhance the system's responsiveness while minimizing overshoot to the greatest extent possible. Using MATLAB and Simulink joint simulation, the PID parameters are tuned using the selfish group optimization algorithm. The test results show that for small set value changes (such as 25% of the full stroke), the system has excellent tracking performance in different stroke segments, can quickly reach the set value without overshoot; For situations where the set value changes greatly (such as 50% of the full stroke), the system can also quickly reach the set value with only slight overshoot. The simulation results show that this scheme can efficiently tune the optimal PID parameters based on the designed objective function and the designed controller has a significant effect in avoiding overshoot and speed.

articleTitle: Analog circuit fault diagnosis method using auto-encoder based feature extraction
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Motivated by the development of artificial intelligence, data-driven fault diagnosis for analogue circuits has become popular. Data-driven methods commonly include two stages: the feature extraction stage and the fault isolation stage. Traditional feature extraction methods, mainly using signal processing, suffer from the problem of information loss and are highly dependent on prior knowledge. In order to deal with the limitations above, a semi-supervised representation learning method is proposed for fault diagnosis. An autoencoder-based structure is adopted to establish a mathematical encoder. The proposed encoder can directly capture the latent feature from the original signal data without traditional data processing. And then a two-layer neural network is applied to further fault classification task. Experiments on two classical filter circuits are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness and merits of the proposed fault diagnosis method for analogue circuits.

articleTitle: Research on acoustic temperature field hotspot tracking based on RBFNN adaptive grid
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Acoustic tomography (AT) is an effective non-contact temperature distribution visualization technique. Most existing acoustic temperature measurement reconstruction algorithms are developed in relatively uniform temperature distribution environments, with less consideration given to acoustic reconstruction of temperature fields with extreme centre concentration and hotspot tracking problem. In order to improve the ability of acoustic tomography imaging to track temperature field hotspots, this paper established an acoustic temperature field reconstruction model based on an improved radial basis function neural network using AT technology. In addition, we proposed a grid partitioning and point layout scheme based on temperature gradient adaptation. When establishing the neural network model using this method, a polynomial was added as a correction term in the hidden layer to establish an improved radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) acoustic temperature field reconstruction model. Based on temperature gradient information without increasing computational complexity, Volonoi polygon embedding rule is applied to adaptively mesh the measurement area, complete the radial basis function centre point layout, reconstruct the temperature field, and track hotspots. Through numerical simulation, this method can effectively visualize the temperature field information when hotspots move to different positions. We reconstructed the temperature field hotspots on the self-developed acoustic temperature measurement experimental system and successfully detected the imaging of hotspots when the heater was moved by 0.25 meters. Simulation and experiments have shown that this acoustic method can effectively track hotspots.

articleTitle: Design of in-line-of-sight dynamic wireless time comparison system based on pseudo-code ranging
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, more and more occasions need to achieve nanosecond time comparison between mobile platforms, such as missile launch vehicles, ships, and other mobile platforms. However, the traditional time comparison technique is mostly applied in static environments. Based on the principle of pseudo-code ranging and bidirectional time comparison, this paper has designed a set of high-precision wireless time comparison systems suitable for dynamic environments. At the same time, in order to solve the problem of large noise and abnormal values in the measurement of the clock bias in the pseudo-range dynamic time ratio, the optimal estimate of the clock bias is obtained by Kalman filtering. Finally, a vehicle-mounted test platform was built to verify the effect of dynamic time comparison. The experimental results show that the dynamic time comparison accuracy is better than 1ns in the range of 1 km.

articleTitle: Hybrid-driven model for temperature prediction in wet clutches
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: A hybrid-driven model for predicting the temperature at the friction interface of wet clutch friction components was developed, employing a radial basis function neural network algorithm. This model uses temperature data obtained from wet clutch test bench experiments to compensate for the results from a thermo-mechanical coupled numerical simulation model of the friction components. The hybrid model inputs include load pressure, relative speed, radial position of the friction components, and numerically simulated temperatures at the friction interface, to output predicted temperatures under specific operating conditions. The results indicate that the predicted temperatures of the friction components under various conditions align well with experimental values, with a maximum mean relative error of 0.033 and all prediction intervals having a coefficient of determination higher than 0.97. Thus, the hybrid-driven model demonstrates high accuracy and stability in predictions, and possesses strong adaptability and predictive capabilities for different temperature distributions at the friction interface.

articleTitle: Hand-to-eye calibration of a robotic arm using point cloud registration method
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to investigate a hand-eye calibration approach employing an eye-to-hand configuration, focusing on point cloud registration. In the initial segments of the paper, the paper delineate the core principles that underpin hand-eye calibration, as well as the various techniques that are predominantly utilized in this field. Furthermore, the article meticulously analyzes the limitations of the traditional methods and identifies potential areas where improvements can be made. Subsequently, it delves into the hand-eye calibration methodology grounded in 3D point cloud registration. This exploration includes an in-depth analysis of an enhanced version of the Super 4PCS Algorithm-based point cloud registration algorithm, which is a novel and effective method for point cloud registration. Additionally, the article discusses the intricacies of coordinate system transformation and provides a comprehensive explanation of how to solve the hand-eye calibration equation AX=XB using the navy method. Furthermore, the paper empirically validates the efficacy and precision of this method. This validation process involves a comparative analysis with other existing approaches. Lastly, it summarizes the research findings and discusses the strengths and limitations of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Application of adaptive particle filter to shipborne cold atom gravimetry
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Shipborne cold atom gravimetry is crucial for geodesy, geophysics, resource exploration and autonomous navigation. Under dynamic conditions, effective reduction of measurement noise is one of the key factors in improving the performance of gravimeter. This study innovatively applied Adaptive Particle Filter (APF) algorithm to shipborne cold atom gravimetry which can effectively reduce measurement noise. This APF algorithm was utilized with offset, contrast of fringe and absolute gravity as its state vectors to observe the output of absolute gravimeter. After filtering the measured atom interference fringes, the optimal estimation of absolute gravity is obtained. This method reduces the dispersion of gravity from 42.1 mGal to 13.6 mGal (T = 5 ms), which is 67.7% less than without algorithm. Meanwhile absolute gravity has almost the same change trend. This result confirms the potential of APF algorithm to for enhancing the performance of absolute shipborne gravimetry.

articleTitle: Design of an electromagnetically tuned mass damper and its experimental study on vibration reduction for flywheel rotor systems
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The trend towards higher speeds in flywheel energy storage systems is highlighting the need for improved bearing support. To overcome the limitations of traditional oil dampers, such as narrow damping range and insufficient damping, this study introduces an Electromagnetic Tuned Mass Damper (ETMD) designed for high-speed, low-inertia flywheel systems. Using Comsol finite element software, a model was created to optimize the damper's parameters. A comparative experiment was conducted between the newly designed ETMD and a conventional oil damper on vibration damping single point flexible support. The experimental findings indicate that a uniform arrangement of permanent magnets within the eddy current damper yields greater damping forces, with the damping coefficient significantly increasing at amplitudes beyond 0.2 mm, and notably effective in controlling low-frequency vibrations within the 75 Hz to 25 Hz range. Although the magnetic yoke is crucial, variations in its thickness minimally affect performance, and the optimal damping effect is achieved with a back iron thickness of 4mm, highlighting the existence of an ideal thickness for the back iron. Rotor experiments have demonstrated that eddy current dampers demonstrate enhanced vibration control with amplitudes of 49 μm, outperforming hydrodynamic dampers at 75 μm during acceleration and 71 μm during deceleration.

articleTitle: Structural reliability analysis based on improved parallel sampling algorithm
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of computational inefficiency of traditional reliability analysis methods when dealing with large-scale structural systems, this paper proposes a reliability analysis method that improves the parallel sample algorithm. The method adopts the Kriging model to fit the performance function and introduces the mean square error to evaluate the uncertainty of the sample points; In addition, the positional relationship between the sample points is taken into consideration to avoid overfitting the model; To improve the efficiency of the model fitting, the sample points are divided into multiple clusters using the Mini batch k-means clustering algorithm in parallel computation. Finally, it is verified by multiple random variable cases that the method can significantly improve the computational efficiency while guaranteeing the relative error compared with other reliability analysis methods.

articleTitle: The adaptive MPC controller of autonomous driving formula for trajectory tracking
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Autonomous driving technology has gradually been applied in real life, and it has also been improved in the China Collegiate Electric Vehicle Racing. However, as one of the critical components of autonomous driving technology, trajectory tracking control still faces challenges. This paper designs a trajectory tracking controller by building a vehicle's three-degree-of-freedom dynamics model and adopting adaptive model predictive control. It adjusts the prediction horizon of the vehicle's trajectory tracking controller in real-time based on the curvature of the desired trajectory to improve the effect of trajectory tracking. Experimental results show that the tracking effect of the adaptive prediction time-domain trajectory tracking controller in the S-curve is improved by 4.97% and 11.36% compared to the fixed prediction time-domain trajectory tracking controller, respectively. For the formula track conditions, the tracking effect of the controller proposed in this paper is improved by 0.71% compared to the fixed prediction time-domain trajectory tracking controller, with an average tracking error of 5.65%.

articleTitle: Research on semantic segmentation based on improved BiSeNet on unstructured road
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Semantic segmentation is very important for unmanned vehicles on unstructured roads. While accuracy of current algorithms is not high enough especially long distance or tiny objects identification and classification which can lead serious accidents. And the parameters used in calculation are so more as well. This paper proposes a semantic segmentation algorithm based on the BiSeNet model. A lightweight network model MobileNetV3-large is employed as the feature extraction network. Additionally, an RFB module is introduced to increase the receptive field and obtain more global information. The CBAM-FFM module is utilized to combine spatial and channel attention mechanisms feature fusion as well. Experimental results show that the improved model achieves an accuracy of 97.47% on the IDD dataset while reducing the model parameters to 3.05×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>. Moreover, it exhibits certain generalization performance on a self-made dataset. Compared to other current semantic segmentation models, the proposed model shows enhanced accuracy, thereby providing important technical support for the practical application of unmanned vehicle on complex unstructured roads.

articleTitle: Application of wavelet kurtosis convolutional neural network model in rolling bearing fault diagnosis
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of substantial noise in the actual industrial environment, where the intelligent diagnostic model exhibits weak anti-noise performance and the interpretability of the extracted features is not strong, the wavelet kurtosis convolutional neural network model integrating signal processing technology and deep learning neural networks has been proposed. Firstly, the standard CNN convolution kernel has been replaced with a wavelet basis function to form a wavelet convolution layer, and the input signal undergoes decomposition into various frequency components via the wavelet filter in this layer; Secondly, a kurtosis loss layer has been used to filter the high kurtosis value components that contain more fault features, so as to achieve the filtration of the noise and the accurate localisation of the fault signals; Lastly, the efficacy of the proposed model has been verified in the rolling bearing dataset and diagnostic model. The results showed that the model can reach 90% diagnostic accuracy under -4db Gaussian white noise interference, which was higher than other diagnostic models, and had good generalisation and noise resistance.

articleTitle: SOH uncertainty estimation for lithium-ion battery packs based on cell inconsistency
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In recent years, lithium-ion battery packs are widely used in several fields. State of health (SOH) of lithium-ion battery packs is a key parameter for evaluating the degradation of their performance. For battery packs, in addition to internal cell degradation, cell inconsistency also has a significant impact on the aging process, leading to more complex degradation and greater uncertainty in the SOH estimation. This paper extracts degradation features based on cell inconsistency and performs uncertainty modelling of battery pack SOH. Six single degradation parameters based on cell inconsistency are extracted using parameters such as monitorable voltage and time interval. In order to reduce the information redundancy of single degradation features and improve the features accuracy, the degradation features are fused using the kernel principal components analysis (KPCA) algorithm. The SOH estimation model of the battery pack is established based on long short-term memory (LSTM) network. The model utilizes a parallel training strategy to quantify the uncertainty in the estimation results. The experimental results based on real battery test data show that the correlation between degradation features and battery capacity is between 0.98 and 0.99, and the error of SOH estimation is less than 0.06, and 95% confidence interval is given.

articleTitle: A new kind of simultaneous measurement of temperature and strain optical fiber grating
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel type of optical fiber grating capable of simultaneous temperature and strain measurement. The grating is fabricated using the ultraviolet lithography method, involving the removal of photosensitivity from a small section of the fiber prior to writing the grating using electrode discharge. The phase shift grating formed by this method is used as an optical fiber sensor to measure the temperature and stress simultaneously which result exhibits two peaks with distinct sensitivities to temperature and strain. Experimental results demonstrate that phase-shifted Bragg grating made by this method enables accurate simultaneous measurement of temperature and strain, which solves the problem of cross-sensitivity of traditional fiber grating.

articleTitle: Research on DC charger on-site calibration based on dc comparator technology
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: A lightweight portable DC charger on-site calibration instrument based on DC comparator technology was studied to address the difficulties in equipment handling, complex operation wiring, high investment in manpower and material resources, time-consuming and laborious calibration process, and low detection efficiency in on-site measurement and testing of DC chargers. An improved Lagrangian phase compensation algorithm is adopted to correct the electrical energy measurement errors caused by the asynchronous voltage and current channels in the dynamic distortion load during DC charging, effectively suppressing the DC energy measurement errors caused by the inconsistent phase delay of voltage and current channels in ripple environments; Design a DC comparator with a dual iron core structure to achieve high-precision measurement of high DC current. The device has higher internal integration, smaller size, lighter weight, and an error of 0.05 level. Moreover, it is compared with the 0.05 level DC energy measurement standard, and the | En | ≤ 1 of multiple comparison data sets. The results show that the developed on-site calibration instrument has accurate and reliable measurement errors, and can be used for on-site measurement of DC chargers. This will greatly improve the efficiency of on-site measurement and ensure the smooth progress of the charging pile inspection work.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation method for measuring crack width of tunnel lining detection instruments
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Ensuring the accuracy of tunnel lining inspection instruments is crucial for maintaining tunnel safety. Given the complexity and variability of lining crack morphologies and widths, it is particularly important to conduct more in-depth verification of the measurement performance of existing tunnel lining crack detection instruments. To this end, our study carefully crafted standardized simulated crack boards using rigid plastic and restored crack morphologies by designing specific skeleton lines. These crack boards not only lay a solid foundation for theoretically calculating crack widths but also provide an innovative method for evaluating the performance of lining crack detection equipment. To create differentiated crack widths and establish their standard values, we designed seven straight lines with varying slopes on the edges of the plastic boards to form the skeleton lines of the cracks and precisely adjusted the spacing between them. Furthermore, this study introduces a new method of stratified data analysis, comparing calibrated and measured values and their relative errors through statistical analysis to verify the measurement stability of the equipment. The research results show that the equipment can effectively identify various crack widths. However, when measuring narrower cracks (<0.20 mm), the relative error of the equipment is relatively high (reaching 48.50%). Nevertheless, when measuring cracks with widths between 0.4 and 0.6 mm, the relative error is significantly reduced to 11.55%. For cracks wider than 0.60 mm, the error is stably controlled below 5%. These findings underscore the central role of standardized crack boards in tunnel lining inspection, enhancing the accuracy and reliability of the inspection process and facilitating consistent inspection results. Through this standardized crack simulation approach, we can provide more reliable data support for the maintenance and evaluation of tunnel linings, ultimately improving overall tunnel safety.

articleTitle: A novel design of closed-loop drive of MEMS gyroscope based on LADRC controller
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) gyroscopes have stringent requirements in terms of control accuracy and system stability. The traditional PI control is widely used in the closed-loop drive loop of MEMS gyroscopes, but the parameters need to be finely tuned to achieve optimal performance. In order to simplify the complexity of parameter tuning and improve the stability and anti-interference ability of the system, a MEMS gyroscope driving closed-loop system based on Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (LADRC) is proposed in this paper. The demodulated output signals with the same reference amplitude are inputted to the LADRC controller to predict the tracking total perturbation, and the control signals are generated to drive the system. Simulation results show that the phase margin of the system is significantly improved by using the LADRC controller approach, the stabilisation time is improved by a factor of 7.5 and the phase margin is improved by a factor of 45°. Simulation results show that the LADRC control contributes to the stability of the control system compared to the PI controlled approach. The simulation further verifies that a wide range of changes in the parameters of the LADRC controller does not affect the system stability, but improves the system's anti-interference capability.

articleTitle: Multifunction radar signal sorting method based on data field and Finch-Means
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In addressing the issues faced by traditional signal sorting methods and clustering algorithms in complex electromagnetic environments, such as the need for prior knowledge, initial center selection, and signal batch increment, a multifunctional radar signal sorting method based on Data Field and Finch-Means is proposed. Initially, the integration of the signal envelope "pulse leading edge" in the radar pulse signal fingerprint features into the Pulse Descriptor Word (PDW) is proposed, forming a new feature parameter (EPDW) used by the Data Field for the elimination of interference pulses. Concurrently, a K-means clustering algorithm based on the first-neighbor points (Finch-Means) is introduced. This algorithm employs the Finch algorithm to calculate the first neighbor vectors of the filtered pulses, preclassify the data, determine the number of clusters, and identify the initial cluster centers. Finally, the K-Means algorithm computes the distances from the pulses to each cluster center and assigns them to the nearest cluster center, completing the final sorting. Simulation experiments show that the average recognition rate of this algorithm reaches 97.85%. Compared to existing methods, the average correct recognition rate of a single radar improves by 14.88%, and the average recognition rate increases by 16.55%.

articleTitle: Structure design of industrial robot feeding and detecting workstation based on vision measurement principle
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In order to reasonable plan the spatial layout of an industrial robot feeding and loading inspection production line based on visual measurement principles and improve the efficiency of industrial robot feeding and inspection, this paper proposes a structural design of an industrial robot feeding and loading inspection workstation based on visual measurement principles. The design content includes: designing the structure of the feeding robot arm, designing the wrist, lower arm, upper arm, lumbar seat, and base of the robotic arm, and selecting the end effector of the robotic arm. Analyze and design the overall plan of the feeding workstation, design the visual workstation, select the conveying mechanism, and select the three jaw chuck. On this basis, briefly describe the working principles of the feeding robot arm and the industrial robot loading inspection workstation. Finally, finite element analysis of stress and deformation of key components such as the upper arm, lower arm, and wrist was conducted using the 3D modeling software Solid Work. The experimental results showed that the industrial robot loading inspection workstation and robotic arm structure designed in this paper meet the design requirements.

articleTitle: Structural design of a small module spur cylindrical gear measuring instrument based on machine vision measurement
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In response to the demand for fast and high-precision measurement of small and medium-sized module spur gears, this paper develops a machine vision based measurement instrument for small and medium-sized module spur gears. The system includes two parts: the mechanical structure of the measuring instrument and the visual measuring device. Among them, the mechanical structure includes the selection of high-precision angle indexing plates, fixture structure design and strength verification, column and marble platform design and verification, as well as the design of X, Y, and Z axis position adjustment mechanisms; The visual measurement device includes: camera lens, CCD camera, LED backlight, and selection of data acquisition card. On this basis, the working principle and design steps of a small module spur cylindrical gear measuring instrument based on machine vision measurement are discussed; Finally, models were constructed for key components such as the core shaft, X-axis lead screw, Y-axis lead screw, and Z-axis lead screw, and finite element analysis was conducted using SoildWorks software. The experimental results showed that this method can meet the design requirements.

articleTitle: A fast calibration and testing method for large-scale phased array
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of long time consuming during the calibration and scanning patterns testing of large-scale phased arrays, a fast-testing method and a verification circuit is proposed in this paper. This method no longer requires the use of expensive vector network analyser (VNA), but uses a lower cost downconverter and sampling board. The downconverter converts the received RF signal into a lower IF signal, then samples and calculates the amplitude and phase of the IF signal using the sampling board. The proposed method is used to calibrate a SATCOM phased array of 1024 channels. After calibration, the RMS value of phase residual errors is less than 2°, and the RMS value of amplitude residual errors is less than 0.26dB. The calibration time using this method is about 2.2 s, while the time using traditional VNA is about 248.7 s. Compared with the traditional testing methods, this design method can significantly reduce the time and cost of measurement, which is very suitable for the testing of large-scale phased arrays. In addition, the proposed method can also be used as a basic step for other further performance tests to improve test efficiency.

articleTitle: Development and engineering application data analysis of automatic inclinometer
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In response to the problems of low measurement efficiency and high manpower investment in traditional manual inclination measurement, a new automatic inclinometer is developed in this paper. On the basis of the slip inclinometer, this instrument has added a set of devices for automatic winding, automatic flipping, and automatic recording, achieving functions such as self-control, self-collection, and self-transmission. The automatic inclinometer has the characteristics of fast measurement speed, low power consumption, and good weather resistance, making it suitable for long-term outdoor work. The device has been operating successfully for more than one year in a horizontal deformation monitoring project for slopes at a hydropower station. The analysis of engineering application data shows that the instrument has high measurement accuracy, good stability, and the potential to replace manual labor and achieve fully automatic inclination measurement.

articleTitle: Calibration study of a silicon drift detector on a monoenergetic X-ray radiation device
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: A monoenergy X-ray calibration setup based on Bragg diffraction has the advantages of continuous energy adjustability and excellent monochromaticity, which can provide detailed calibration experiments for detectors with selectable energies. Monte Carlo simulation software was used to simulate the detection efficiency of the silicon drift detector, obtaining the detection efficiency in the (10~40) keV energy band. Calibration experiments for the detection efficiency of the silicon drift detector were carried out on a monoenergetic X-ray calibration setup, and the experimentally measured detection efficiencies were obtained which were compared with the simulated efficiency curves. The error between the experimental and simulated results is minimized to 4.63 % at 40 keV. Factors affecting the calibration experiment include whether the beam spot is completely received by the detector and the shielding effect of the detector itself. The detection efficiency of the silicon drift detector can be improved by reducing the aperture of the beam-limiting diaphragm in the future.

articleTitle: A study of capicitance characteris of metal micro-hemispherical resonant gyro detection
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Compared with the traditional quartz hemispherical resonant gyro, the metal micro hemispherical resonant gyro has a stronger high overload capacity and can adapt to more extreme environments, and its capacitance characteristics directly determine the performance of the metal micro hemispherical resonant gyro. In this paper, an oscillator with a diameter of 12 mm is selected, and the capacitance characteristics of the metal micro hemispherical resonant gyro are studied in detail from the two influencing factors of the number of oscillator teeth and capacitance spacing. The finite element simulation of the oscillator has been carried out using finite element software and the capacitive characteristics have been simulated and analyzed. The results show that when the number of teeth of the oscillator is 16 teeth and the capacitance spacing is 0.05 mm, the excited area is enhanced by 460% and the capacitance value increases to 10 pF. This study provides an important theoretical basis for the capacitance design of the resonant gyro with a metal micro hemisphere.

articleTitle: The technology research of the airplane stick (helm) force field testing calibration
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In the face of the test environment and requirement change on the plane, laboratory testing calibration method of the force parameter has been unable to meet the requirement of the present. According to the principle of force sensor, developed a new test method that can realize field calibration of the airplane stick (helm) force parameters. This article firstly has carried on the demand analysis of the airplane stick (helm) force field on-line testing calibration and finds out the key points and difficulties. Finally, we adopt this method which applies pull and pressure at the same time on the standard force sensor and the airplane stick (helm) by the special fixture, and at the same time for data acquisition. Getting the test results, the precision of the two parameters are not more than 1%. It can meet the test requirements, and demonstrates the feasibility and correctness of the test method.

articleTitle: Smoking behavior detection based on improved YOLOv7 object association
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: To address the security risks caused by unauthorized individuals smoking in public places, a method for detecting smoking behavior based on an improved YOLOv7 target association is proposed. First, the improved YOLOv7 algorithm is used to detect the people and cigarette targets in the image, and then the distance relationship between the center coordinates of the cigarette target detection frame and the person target detection box is calculated, and the correlation between the two is located to determine whether there is smoking behavior. The improved YOLOv7 algorithm introduces the CBAM attention module to prioritize key areas and diminish background interference. Simultaneously, the SIOU loss function is employed to bolster the precision of the regression outcomes. Experiments conducted on the test dataset reveal that the proposed approach achieves an accuracy of 91.35% and a detection speed of 78 FPS, achieving real-time accurate detection effects.

articleTitle: Development of high-precision automatic evaporation monitoring device
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: This study proposed a novel liquid level measurement mode, which applies high-precision liquid level measurement sensors to the measurement of water surface evaporation. Through a data acquisition controller, the entire process of monitoring water surface evaporation, including changes in evaporator water level, rainfall, replenishment, and drainage, is collected, recorded, and transmitted, achieving fully automatic online and accurate measurement of water surface evaporation. The device adopts automatic replenishment and drainage mode and advanced sensing measurement technology, which can effectively avoid the observation error caused by overflow and rainfall. According to the application data of the device in a hydrological station, the device has a higher qualified rate than the artificial observation of daily evaporation, which can replace the artificial observation of water surface evaporation method and improve the efficiency of hydrological monitoring.

articleTitle: Performance optimization of high altitude humidity sensor based on dynamic calibration and compensation
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: High-altitude humidity measurement is crucial for weather forecasting, climate change research, and aerospace activities. However, the extreme environmental conditions of the upper atmosphere, including low temperatures, low pressures, and strong radiation, pose significant challenges to the performance of humidity sensors. Therefore, studying the optimization methods for high-altitude humidity sensors under sub-zero temperature conditions is of great importance. This paper focuses on the performance optimization of high-altitude humidity sensors and conducts research based on dynamic calibration and compensation. A humidity dynamic parameter calibration system has been constructed, providing an experimental platform for the dynamic calibration of high-altitude humidity sensors. Correcting models have been established to address the impact of parameters such as temperature and wind speed on high-altitude humidity measurement results, and the models have been verified using sounding test data, improving the response time and data quality of high-altitude humidity measurements. This research will involve the dynamic characteristics of a large number of other types of humidity sensors in the future. Through continuous research and improvement, it will provide more accurate and reliable technical support for high-altitude humidity measurement, which has important theoretical significance and practical value in the fields of meteorological sounding, meteorological observation, and aerospace.

articleTitle: An AFDX data collection module based on miniVPX
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: As aviation technology advances, planes are becoming larger and more efficient, resulting in a greater volume of data that has to be handled. Conventional communication protocols such as ARINC429, ARINC629, and MIL-STD-1553B are no longer sufficient in terms of data transfer speed and quality. This design seeks to create a compact AFDX (Avionics Full Duplex Switched Ethernet) data collection module using the miniVPX platform, in accordance with the ARINC specification 664. The module adheres to the P2 section about the physical layer and the P7 section concerning the data link layer in the ARINC specification 664. The text primarily presents the logical firmware and techniques for implementing the functions of the data link layer. These operations, as outlined in the P7 section of the ARINC specification 664, encompass Integrity Checking and Redundancy Management. Simultaneously, it possesses a user configuration interface and has the capability to modify its operational state in real-time. The simulation verification demonstrates that the planned AFDX data collection module is capable of achieving real-time and predictable communication in AFDX networks.

articleTitle: Design of digital filter with variable cutoff frequency based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Digital filter is a module often used in engineering design. In order to design more flexible filter, a scheme of digital filter with variable cutoff frequency is proposed. A digital filter is designed by using FPGA technology. The upper computer sends the control instruction of the end frequency to the FPGA, which is extracted by the front-end extractor to reduce the sampling rate, and then performs 100-order FIR filtering operation with the filter coefficient, and performs truncation processing after the operation. Then the signal is interpolated to restore the sampling rate of the signal, and the truncation is processed again after the interpolation. The test results show that the filter can convert the cutoff frequency in a large range, the filter has simple flow, good filtering effect, wide application range and strong flexibility, and can help engineers to solve many engineering problems.

articleTitle: RSSI-based injected ground current field localization study
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that traditional positioning techniques are easily limited in complex environments, this study proposes a positioning method based on Received Signal Strength Indication (RSSI) of injected ground current field, which is suitable for closed or sheltered environments, such as underground alleyways, and also works effectively under extreme conditions, such as alleyways collapsing. Firstly, the validity of the ground current field signals is tested to ensure that the signals are reliable; secondly, the extracted signals are screened to remove signals with low signal-to-noise ratios and high ground resistance, and to reduce the influence of environmental noise on the localization results; next, the RF parameter A as well as the signal transmission constant n are computed using the linear regression least square method, which provide important fitting parameters for the subsequent establishment of the RSSI localization model; finally, a Gaussian filtering to process the RSSI data collected by modelling. The experimental results show that the method achieves the positioning of underground alleyways environment with good feasibility and effectiveness, and provides a feasible solution for carrying out efficient alleyway personnel positioning and rescue operations, which has important theoretical significance and practical value.

articleTitle: Nonlinear steam generator feedwater system identification based on wavelet neural network
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Steam generator is the key equipment in the large and complex nuclear power plant, and its water supply system has the characteristics of time-varying, large delay, nonlinear. In this paper, a segmented linearized model based on wavelet neural network is developed for a steam generator feedwater system of a nuclear power plant. All the data of the automation stages of the steam generator, which are steam flow rate, feedwater flow rate and liquid level from 20% load to 100% load, are collected and divided into six stages based on the characteristics of the data. For the first four stages of data, the feedwater system was modelled using the Hammerstein-Wiener method based on wavelet neural network, which was used as the nonlinear input and nonlinear output module of Hammerstein-Wiener. And for the remaining two stages of data, the nonlinear autoregressive models based on with exogenous (ARX) inputs model approach was modelled using nonlinear ARX as the underlying framework of wavelet neural network. The proposed model can be used for model predictive control to switch between different models based on load changes. Through the verification of simulation experiments, the built model can accurately reflect the trend of actual data, and the predicted values have high accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Decoupling and preparation of flexible haptic three-dimensional force sensor
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: An asymmetric capacitive haptic sensor structure with three-dimensional force detection capability has been designed. The sensor unit comprises a upper public electrode, three under electrode plates and fork finger electrodes. Developed a visualization interface for this system by PyQt5. A series of tests were conducted on the sensor, including tensile and flex fatigue tests, single and dynamic pressure performance tests, tangential force performance tests and three-dimensional force tests. The response time of the sensor was found to be 3.5 seconds, while the recovery time was 5.5 seconds. The sensitivity of the Z-axis was 0.081 Kpa<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>in the range of 0 to 4.22 Kpa and 0.014 Kpa<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>in the range of 4.22 to 29.31 Kpa, the sensitivities in the positive and negative directions of the X-axis was 0.223 pF/N and -0.248 pF/N, while the sensitivities in the positive and negative directions of the Y-axis was 0.242 pF/N and -0.243 pF/N. The tests demonstrates that the sensor exhibited satisfactory flexibility, repeatability, and a linearity of 0.16%, thereby ensuring reliable measurement outcomes.

articleTitle: Half-duplex underwater communication system with broadband high-frequency transducer
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: High-speed, short-range communication has important applications in the field of underwater communication and in the field of medicine. We have designed a comprehensive half-duplex underwater communication system with a high-frequency broadband transducer, which includes complete hardware design and software design. The baud rate of the system can adjust from 1 KBaud to 30 KBaud, and the carrier waveform is 150 kHz to 200 kHz. The user can adjust the above parameters through the PC software according to the specific usage situation. Each module has been tested in a water tank. When the transducer is operated at the optimum frequency of 171 kHz, the system is capable of communicating accurately from 10 kbps to 25 kbps in the water tank in simplex mode. In half-duplex mode, communication rates of 10 kbps to 20 kbps can be achieved. The whole system realises the functions of distance measurement and temperature measurement. Our design provide a solution for short-range ultra-high-speed communication.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a deep learning-based quality detection system for cork discs
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: High-quality badminton shuttlecock heads are made from cork discs derived from natural oak bark, which exhibit complex cracks and wrinkles, causing inefficiency and inconsistency in quality screening. To address this, we propose a deep learning-based detection algorithm using YOLOv5. The YOLOv5 model was optimized for cork disc characteristics by introducing an attention mechanism to enhance feature representation and designing a post-processing algorithm to improve detection accuracy. The optimized model, trained on a custom cork disc dataset using an NVIDIA RTX3080 GPU, achieved 86.7% mF1 and 81.5% mAP, outperforming other mainstream algorithms. Finally, the system utilizes Nvidia's edge computing device Jetson Nano as the computational core, deploying the YOLOv5 model and designing the graphical interface on Ubuntu 18.04. Real-time cork disc image acquisition is achieved using binocular industrial cameras and fiber optic sensors, while a uniformly rotating turntable and diversion device are designed to facilitate the transfer of cork disc. Experimental results show that the system achieves a 92.75% classification accuracy for four quality grades with an inference time of 87.6ms, meeting the requirements for real-time cork disc quality inspection.

articleTitle: State observers for output feedback control of electro-hydraulic systems
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Electro-hydraulic systems are the updated version of conventional valve-controlled hydraulics. This actuation technology, which is crucial in many fields of industry, still has room for improvement in some areas. In this regard, feedback control is challenging as only the hydraulic actuator's position and pressure drop are typically measured for practical reasons.
