Thus, our focus is on constructing a state observer because knowing all the system’s state variables, including the actuator velocity, is desirable for achieving effective closed-loop position control. We propose a feedback linearization approach for output feedback control by developing an observer relying only on the measured position and pressures. We leverage linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) to obtain a proper observer gain. This unconventional approach for electro-hydraulic drives leads to satisfactory observer behavior. Therefore, this contribution further establishes electro-hydraulic systems by proposing novel alternatives to facilitate their control.

articleTitle: Advance in study of safety monitoring methods for nuclear power plants
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: There are numerous monitoring objects and various monitoring methods for NPPs. In order to master the monitoring methods and their progress, and provide a basis and reference for the research and design of monitoring systems for NPPs, this paper analyses the research progress of monitoring methods from the aspects of system, equipment, objects, structure, operation, and environment. The analysis results show that the monitoring of NPP systems, equipment, objects, and structures has expanded from traditional parameter and fault monitoring to fault prediction and diagnosis; Extend from equipment performance and fault monitoring to equipment aging monitoring and management; Expanding from usage monitoring to full life monitoring; Developing from monitoring device performance and faults to monitoring and managing device health status. The research on operational monitoring of NPPs is gradually advancing from parameter monitoring and operational status monitoring to operational fault prediction, fault diagnosis, intelligent monitoring, and comprehensive monitoring. The main development of environmental monitoring for NPPs is the research and application of robot monitoring technology. Intelligent monitoring, prediction, diagnosis, and analysis are important research and development directions for safety monitoring of NPPs.

articleTitle: Design of a universal active passive composite safety control system for target missiles
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The safety control system in weapons and equipment is directly related to the safety of personnel and property, and can effectively improve the safety of flight experiments. It is an indispensable and important component of weapons and equipment. The target missile safety control system directly determines whether the target missile can self destruct in case of abnormal flight conditions, so it is of great significance for interception flight experiments. With the gradual development of domestic safety technology and the increasing number of flight experiments, the safety requirements for flight experiments in shooting ranges are becoming higher and higher. There is a trend in technical requirements from active safety to active passive composite safety. This article provides an overview of the working principles of commonly used safety control systems and designs a composite safety control system that combines active and passive methods. A comprehensive system design is carried out from the aspects of overall architecture, hardware scheme, safety logic, etc. Two levels of ground testing schemes, single machine testing and system level testing, are designed for the system to ensure the safety and reliability of the universal target missile active and passive composite safety control system.

articleTitle: Railway intruding pedestrian image sequence generation method with pose transfer techniques
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Pedestrians intruding detection on deep learning method is vital for the safety of high-speed railway operations. The accuracy of deep learning object recognition is significantly depended on the volume and diversity of training samples. Addressing the issue of insufficient and hard-to-obtain intruding images in high-speed railway scenes, this paper introduces a novel method for generating railway intruding pedestrian image sequences with pose transfer. This method can generate necessary intruding samples and produce the annotated files automatically for deep learning training. To tackle the challenges of pose feature extraction, a pose transfer module based on generative adversarial network is proposed; furthermore, a feature fusion module based on spatial attention mechanisms has been proposed to preserve essential pose features. Experimental results on the DeepFashion dataset demonstrate that the proposed modules significantly enhance the quality of generated pedestrian images and the accuracy of pose transfer. In the same data set, compared with the classical pose transfer algorithm, the algorithm in this paper improves the SSIM index by 5.6% and the pckh index by 2.9%. Finally, the effectiveness of the intruding image generatio n is also verified by the improvement of detection algorithm accuracy.

articleTitle: Calibration equipment for defibrillator analyzer designed with digital multimeter and oscilloscope
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Defibrillators use electrical pulses to the heart of patients to make hearts beating normally again. There are mainly 3 types of defibrillators, monophasic wave, biphasic wave, and multipulse biowave. Defibrillator analyzers are designed to calibrate defibrillators, and the pulse energy is an important parameter of defibrillator analyzers. In this manuscript, we use the voltage- resistance method for energy calibration. We need to design a high voltage divider, digitizing module, and data processing project. In the digitizing module, we use both the digital multimeter and the oscilloscope to sample. Making DC voltage measurements is one type of digitizing methods of Keysight 3458A, which uses memory of the multimeter. The process project is developed by VB language with IO Libraries Suite of Keysight to implement the function of digitizing and energy calculation. We also choose NI PXI oscilloscope for digitizing, and the oscilloscope can be calibrated by NI Calibration Executive Software. The process project is developed by LabView. The measurement results by 3458A and PXI-5122 are consistent. We evaluate the uncertainty at the end of this manuscript.

articleTitle: Long-term measurement stability of domestic pavement traffic speed deflectometer
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: With the rapid development of infrastructure, the demand for road maintenance and monitoring work is increasingly urgent. Pavement deflection, as a key indicator of road structural performance, is crucial for engineering quality control. Traditional deflection measurement methods, due to their low efficiency, can no longer meet current needs, while the emergence of laser dynamic deflection measurement technology has brought revolutionary changes to road detection. This paper studies the long-term measurement performance of the domestic pavement Traffic Speed Deflectometer (TSD), especially their accuracy and time stability. The assessment is carried out through two key indicators: repeatability and correlation with the Falling Weight Deflectometer (FWD) measurements. The research found that after five years of use, the tested TSD still shows good measurement repeatability and maintains a high correlation with the FWD measurement results. This indicates that the equipment has excellent long-term stability and reliability, suitable for large-scale road deflection measurement work across the country.

articleTitle: Grid-connected control based on dual compensation-droop for direct-drive PMSG wind power systems
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In order to realize the safe and stable grid-connection of the direct-drive permanent magnet synchronous generator (D-PMSG) used in wind power generation systems, a gird-connected control strategy combined dual-compensation droop and multiple quasi proportional resonance (MQPR) is proposed in this paper. Based on the traditional droop control, a DC voltage compensation is introduced in the voltage control, which can quickly adjust the fluctuation of DC bus voltage. A capacitor current compensation is joined in the current control, which can effectively reduce the impact of current error caused by the filtering capacitor. Meanwhile, a MQPR controller is designed to replace the PI controller for filtering out multiple harmonic currents in the system. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by establishing a simulation model and comparing it with the dual closed-loop PI and traditional droop control strategies.

articleTitle: Experimental study on the vibration characteristics of confluence planetary row in health and broken teeth failure
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: As one of the core components to realize dual-power convergence in the transmission device, the confluence planetary row is characterized by large force and high rotational speed in the actual operation process, and its failure is easy to lead to the failure of straight driving and steering function of the crawler vehicle. The design and construction of the converging planetary row vibration test bench, with the planetary wheel broken teeth fault as an example, respectively, to carry out healthy and broken teeth fault confluence planetary row dynamics characteristics of experimental research, through different loads and different degree of broken teeth faults and other groups of tests, for the groups of experimental results of the data analysis of the time-frequency domain response characteristics of the planetary wheel broken teeth faults to get the characteristics of the vibration of the planetary wheel broken teeth faults, as a confluence planetary row failure identification and diagnosis to provide the basis. The vibration characteristics of planetary wheel broken teeth are obtained to provide a basis for the identification and diagnosis of confluence planetary row fault.

articleTitle: Analysis and comparison of the effect of phase error on three quadrature suppression methods
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The quadrature error caused by micromachining is the key factor affecting the performance of gyroscope. To eliminate the quadrature error, the closed-loop quadrature suppression methods is usually adopted. However, closed-loop quadrature suppression is easily affected by phase errors. This paper analyses and compares the effect of phase error on three quadrature error suppression methods. The composition of zero-rate output of gyroscope after quadrature suppression with phase error is analysed by theoretical derivation. The theoretical analysis results show that there is no quadrature error in the zero-rate output of the quadrature coupling stiffness correction method after quadrature suppression, and the correction effect is the best among the three methods. The experimental results show that the theoretical analysis is correct, and the variation of the zero-rate output in full temperature range of the gyroscope decreases from 0.05 deg/s to less than 0.01 deg/s after the quadrature coupling stiffness correction.

articleTitle: Deep CNN fusing attention and LGBM classifier for high-accuracy hand gesture recognition
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Gesture recognition has been widely used in automation and medical and smart-home. The adaptability and accuracy of traditional machine learning algorithms are limited by feature extraction and classifier selection, and the recognition accuracy is low as well as the robustness is poor. In our work, an improved CNN (Convolutional Neural Networks) combined with an LGBM (Lightweight Gradient Boosting Machine) hand gesture recognition method is proposed to improve the performance of hand gesture recognition. The method designs a 4-layer CNN structure and integrates a CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module) in the network to enhance the model's ability to learn and extract features. Furthermore, the extracted features are fed into an LGBM classifier for gesture classification, which improves the accuracy of gesture classification and reduces the risk of model overfitting. The accuracy of the 16 types of static gesture recognition reaches 97.89% in our dataset. An improvement of more than 10% is obtained in comparison with traditional machine learning classification algorithms. It demonstrates promising prospects for gesture recognition.

articleTitle: Research on artificial intelligence recognition of 3D printer operation conditions based on acoustic signal
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Monitoring the operating condition of the equipment is crucial. This study explores the feasibility of using transfer learning methods and acoustic signals to identify the operating conditions of 3D printers. A sound sensor probe was designed and fabricated to collect acoustic signals generated during the operation of the 3D printer. Sound recognition models based on ResNet34 and transfer learning were constructed to monitor the operating condition of the 3D printer. Comparative experiments demonstrated that the sound recognition model based on transfer learning showed significant improvements in convergence speed and classification accuracy, achieving a classification accuracy of 97.6%. Furthermore, the acoustic signals of the 3D printer were converted into spectrograms and Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients which were then input into the transfer learning model for training. The results indicated that the overall performance of the model was optimal when the input features were spectrograms.

articleTitle: Knowledge graph ontology model construction based on hierarchy structure and failure analysis for wind turbines
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Wind turbines have been widely employed to convert wind kinetic energy into mechanical and end electrical energy as clean and pollution-free renewable energy for handling energy shortages and environmental pollution. In order to better manage and utilize fault knowledge and improve fault diagnosis efficacy of wind turbines, this study constructs a knowledge graph ontology model with system architecture and failure analysis. The model embraces equipment, fault and maintenance knowledge with attribute values in the system-function-motion-action-component (SFMAC) hierarchy structure that is a motion-oriented layered structure division method especially suitable for mechanical systems to obtain the most fundamental and smallest motion of power and motion transmission, namely translation and rotation meta-actions. Equipment knowledge is obtained by the SFMAC hierarchy structure, in which failure analysis integrating fault tree analysis (FTA) and failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) is implemented to map failure behaviors and events and draw failure cause and effect fault trees from the action layer to the component and system layers respectively for garnering fault and maintenance knowledge. The constructed model is more hierarchical, complete and plain to present relationships of equipment, fault and maintenance knowledge in wind turbines.

articleTitle: Structure design of arm exoskeleton robot
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: ARM exoskeleton robot is widely used in rehabilitation medicine, industrial production, military, disability, aerospace and scientific research experiments, and plays an important role. In this paper, an arm exoskeleton robot with multiple joints moving independently is designed, which is aimed at the human upper limb movement, such as forward bending, backward extending, adduction and right bending limit of joints, the design provides the user with auxiliary strength and a degree of upper-body flexibility, which can be used for reference to other arm exoskeletons of the same type. The arm exoskeleton designed in this paper includes Motor I, Worm gear and worm box, Upper arm I, Reducer, Short connector, Motor II, Upper Arm II, Forearm, Motor III, Motor IV, Pinion, Motor screw, the design of the structure and size parameters of the large gear, and the working principle of the arm exoskeleton and the implementation steps are briefly described. On this basis, the paper carries out the structural design and strength check of the key parts such as Worm, Gear, Transmission shaft and so on. Finally, through the finite element analysis, build the key components of the model, stress and deformation analysis and verification, the results show that the method can meet the design requirements.

articleTitle: A study of ionisation chamber energy response measurements based on monoenergetic X-ray
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Ionisation chambers, as an important tool for radiation measurements, are particularly critical in terms of their energy response characteristics, while monoenergetic X-ray have the advantages of continuous and adjustable energy, large injections and good stability compared to conventional radioactive sources. In this study, a high-pressure gas ionisation chamber is measured and its energy response is calculated using a monoenergetic X-ray device, and the data are plotted and compared with those from Monte Carlo simulations to validate the feasibility of the measurement study using a monoenergetic X-ray device. The study proposes to calibrate the energy response of the ionisation chamber by counting with a standard high-purity germanium detector and using the ratio of its omnipotent peak detection efficiency as the true value. The conclusions show that the experimental and simulated curves follow the same trend, with an overall increase with increasing energy, especially in the medium energy region (15 keV-25 keV) where the trends of the normalised energy response curves are roughly in agreement, demonstrating the feasibility of using a monoenergetic X-ray device to measure the energy response of ionisation chambers.

articleTitle: Research progress in fluxgate current sensors for precise measurement
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The current sensor based on the principle of fluxgate is characterized by high linearity, high accuracy and wide frequency band, widely used for precise measurement of AC and DC current. Derive the magnetomotive force balance equation and analyze the excitation current cancellation mechanism. According to the excitation method, the fluxgate current sensor was divided into two types: external excitation type and self excitation type. The research progress at home and abroad was elaborated, including application fields, structural principle, key technical indicators, and main innovation points. Clear principle structure is an advantage of external excitation type, but there are many modules that need to be checked one by one when faults occur. The self excitation type is characterized by the simple circuit and is not limited by the optimal excitation condition. In addition, simplifying the circuit can reduce the failure rate, power consumption, and component temperature drift. Explore the future development trends of fluxgate current sensors and the work to be further studied.

articleTitle: Study of the impact resistance of a self-balancing resistive thermal expanding flow gyroscope
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: We propose thermal expansion flow gyroscopes with self-balancing resistance and study their impact resistance. In this paper, a thermal expansion flow gyro with self-balancing resistors is used as the research basis, aiming to improve the environmental adaptability of the gyro through technological innovation. The thermal expansion flow gyro contains an upper chamber, a lower chamber and a base layer, which contains four thermistors, two heating resistors and two balancing resistors. In order to improve the detection accuracy of the Wheatstone bridge, the balancing resistors and thermistors are fabricated using the same MEMS process, which ensures that the balancing resistors are highly consistent with the thermistors in terms of material, structure, and process, and achieves a high degree of matching and stability. Based on the above analysis, we carried out a finite element analysis of the impact resistance of the self-contained balancing resistor thermal expansion flow gyro. The experimental results show that the impact resistance of this thermal expansion flow gyro can reach 14,752 g when the load is applied in 0~10ms, which fully proves its high stability in harsh environments. The results of this study will provide a reference for subsequent gyro performance studies.

articleTitle: 4MBPS 1553B bus communication card based on MiniVPX architecture
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Aiming at the requirements of miniaturization and integration of aviation test equipment and the problems of complex logic and limited transmission rate of commonly used 1553B bus interface, we propose a design scheme of a high-speed 1553B bus communication card based on MiniVPX architecture, which adopts the LHB155304 as the protocol processing unit with a one-way dual-redundant 1553B channel, and the transmission rate is up to 4 Mbit/s. XC7A200T FPGA is used as the main controller to communicate with LHB155304, and the FPGA realizes data interaction through PCIE bus with CPU in the MiniVPX test equipment. This paper introduces the basic characteristics of the 1553B bus and MiniVPX architecture, and elaborates on the hardware design of the 1553B bus interface, the firmware design of BC mode of 1553B bus, and the implementation of host computer driver software. The designed 1553B bus BC mode is tested and verified, and the results show that the transmission rate of the card communication interface meets the requirement of 4 Mbit/s, and the real-time performance is good, which meets the requirements of engineering application.

articleTitle: Design of high uniformity magnetic field coils for magnetoencephalography measurement
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The uniformity of the central region within a magnetic shielding room (MSR) is a critical factor affecting the accuracy of magnetoencephalography (MEG) measurement. High uniformity coil design is a key technology for obtaining the required magnetic field environment. This paper introduces a design method of the high uniformity planar coil based on bat algorithm (BA), which significantly enhances the uniformity of the target region. Based on the target field method, a dual-plane coil generating uniform magnetic fields in the x, y, and z directions was designed. Each directional coil consists of a primary coil and a secondary coil. The Bat Optimization Algorithm was used to optimize the distances from the primary and secondary coils to the center point. Finally, the coil structure was simulated and analyzed using electromagnetic simulation software. The results demonstrate a substantial improvement in uniformity by 38% and 40% in the Bx (By) and Bz directions, respectively, compared to coils designed using traditional TFMs. Therefore, the coil system designed using this method can provide a better zero magnetic field environment for the signal acquisition of magnetoencephalography (MEG).

articleTitle: Study on coupling fault diagnosis of the planetary transmission gearbox by using wavelet transform and 1DCNN
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Considering the susceptibility of planetary transmission to strong noise interference, a fault diagnosis method is proposed based on Morlet wavelet transform and 1D Convolutional Neural Network (1DCNN). Firstly, the acceleration captured from the transmission is dealt with angle resampling to reduce the dependence of speed on signal characteristics, and band-pass filtering is performed, which parameter is determined by using the fast spectral kurtosis algorithm. Subsequently, the filtered data is decomposed into several multiple intrinsic mode function (IMF) components with the EEMD algorithm and reconstructed according to the correlation coefficient parameter. Then reconstructed data is subjected to further noise reduction processing using wavelet transform and the amplitude in the scale parameter with the highest kurtosis as the input to 1DCNN for training and fault diagnosis classification. The experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively reduce noise interference, the fault diagnosis accuracy of the processed data is relatively high. The fault diagnosis accuracy of the processed data is significantly higher than that of the raw data.

articleTitle: Periodic statistical analysis of gait phase segmentation
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In order to achieve accurate segmentation of gait phases for precise real-time control of lower limb exoskeleton robots, the periodic statistical analysis of human motion posture by using the inertial measurement unit is conducted. In current research, the data of forward and turning gait types were acquired and every gait type data were devised into eight for different gait phase segmentation. During the process, the phase division values for different types of subjects were calculated and the phase division of different subjects with the same gait type was calculated. The standard deviations for different gaits and phases for the same experimenter are all below 10, primarily oscillated around 4. For gait data from different subjects, the percentages at the same phase are all below 3. The results showed that the results from the feasible method could better accord with the characteristics of each stage of actual movement.And those results could provide reference for real-time judgment of gait phase and technical support for intelligent control of lower limb exoskeletons.

articleTitle: Optimal design of accelerated life test with competitive failure products based on function transformation
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Competitive failure is an important failure mode of products, for high reliability, long life, competition failure products, usually using the method of accelerated test to assess the reliability of the product. In recent years, the competitive index distribution failure product accelerated life test optimization design has made great progress, but the Weibull distribution of competitive failure product accelerated life test optimization design is still in the exploratory stage. Due to the complexity of statistical analysis of accelerated data with competitive failure products, the statistical processing of accelerated data of competitive failure products is introduced from the perspective of reliability analysis, the influence of competitive failure mechanism on reliability assessment cannot be ignored, so it is necessary to study the design optimization of accelerated life test with competitive failure products. But it is very difficult to realize design optimization of accelerated life test with competitive failure products under analytical solution. The analytical solution is transformed into the constrained extremal solution of explicit function, and the method of explicit objective function fitting is proposed to realize the optimal design of constant stress accelerated life test with competitive failure products. Through the simulation data, it is concluded that the optimal test scheme has the advantages of feasibility, stability.

articleTitle: Research on prediction of human lower limb joint angle based on sEMG signal
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The lower limb exoskeleton robot is a human-machine collaborative intelligence system that is human-centered. Accurate real-time recognition of human motion intention is a critical technology that must be overcome in developing lower-limb exoskeleton robots. Many studies analyse human motion intention through physiological electrical signals, such as human real-time joint angle, angular velocity, motion acceleration, etc. Surface electromyography (sEMG), as an easy-to-collect human physiological signal, has the advantage of giving full play to its time advancement and behavioral perception globality. In summary, this paper focuses on the mapping relationship between the sEMG signal and human lower limb joint angle to realize the efficient identification of human motion intention and improve the human-machine coordination of lower limb exoskeleton robot. Finally, the model constructed in this paper has the following three advantages. A data set with low redundancy is used as a training set and a test set. Compare the data feature extraction effects of different feature extraction methods for extracting surface electromyography signals, including mean absolute values (MAV), variance (VAR), empirical mode decomposition (EMD), wavelet packet decomposition (WPD). Based on the time series characteristics of surface EMG signals, a time domain neural network is selected to construct a prediction model.

articleTitle: A MEMS-INS error suppression method for vehicle navigation
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: When the navigation satellite signal is interrupted, the integrated INS/GNSS navigation system will be degraded to an independent INS navigation system. Without the assistance by other sensors, the error of the navigation solution will accumulate rapidly with time, which greatly reduces the availability of the navigation system. MEMS IMU is taken as the research object for vehicle navigation, and a method is proposed by converting the knowledge of dynamic models or physical conditions of land moving vehicles into measurement inputs for Kalman filter of integrated navigation systems to suppress the navigation errors based on vehicle velocity and motion state, and the corresponding algorithmic mode is constructed. The proposed method is tested by experimental data, and the experimental results show that both the velocity constraint model and the position constraint model based on vehicle motion can effectively reduce the error accumulation rate of vehicle navigation solutions, and improve the availability and reliability of vehicle MEMS INS independent navigation system.

articleTitle: A synchronous automatic positioning straight cylindrical gear visual measuring instrument
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: This paper designs a synchronous automatic positioning straight cylindrical gear visual measuring instrument, where the internal gears are the main measurement objects and detailed profile analysis is conducted. Compared with traditional contact measurement instruments, this design not only has the advantages of fast measurement speed and high measurement accuracy, but also shows significant advantages in processing the complex shape of the internal gear tooth profile. The components designed in this paper include a high-precision rotating platform mechanism, transmission mechanisms along the X and Y axes, and a self-centering clamping mechanism. In the design process, the core components of the electric control translation stage mechanism, stepping motor, and high-precision rotating platform were selected to ensure the stability and measurement accuracy of the tester. In the process of designing the fixture, special attention was paid to the calculation and verification of the size and strength. Using SolidWorks software, finite element analysis was conducted, and the experimental results showed that the fixture could withstand sufficient force and stability when clamping the internal gear.

articleTitle: Study on the measurement method of ground conductivity of injected ground current field
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The injected ground field technology is crucial for personnel localization and communication in complex geological environments, and accurate acquisition of ground conductivity information is a matter of communication quality and positioning accuracy. Aiming at the limitations of the traditional four-terminal electrode method of laying electrodes, this paper proposes a ground conductivity measurement method with non-linearly laid electrodes. The feasibility of the method was verified and analyzed in a numerical simulation environment. The results show that the method has good feasibility and accuracy, but attention should be paid to the effect of electrode asymmetry on the measurement results in the case of close distance between the detection electrode and the injection electrode. In the field measurement experiments, the standard deviation of the measured data of this method is less than 0.55 us/mm, and the maximum relative error is not more than 8.82%, which is able to meet the needs of the actual project, and provides a feasible solution for the measurement of conductivity under the complex geological environments, especially when the application of the traditional four-terminal electrode method is limited.

articleTitle: Investigation of electromagnetic acoustic transducer efficiency with composite magnetisation direction magnets
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: This study investigates Electromagnetic Acoustic Transducers (EMATs) efficiency with composite magnetisation direction magnets. EMATs are an essential technology for non-destructive testing (NDT) in industrial applications, offering advantages such as non-contact operation and suitability for harsh environments. However, the application of EMATs is often limited by weak testing signals. This research explores the optimisation of bias magnetic fields through various magnet arrangements to enhance transduction efficiency. The study uses finite element simulations to compare magnetic field distributions and their effects on EMAT performance for different magnet configurations, including periodic permanent magnets (PPM), ring-type magnets, and Halbach arrays. Results indicate that specific composite magnet configurations can significantly improve both the normal and tangential magnetic flux density, thereby increasing the strength of the generated and received ultrasonic waves. This optimisation of the bias magnetic field is crucial for advancing EMAT technology and improving testing accuracy in industrial NDT applications.

articleTitle: Research on the fault classification method of rolling bearings based on envelope entropy screening criterion and vmd fusion SVM
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: As a critical component in mechanical equipment, the fault diagnosis of rolling bearings is of great significance. Due to the presence of substantial noise in vibration signals, extracting fault features becomes particularly challenging. This paper proposes a method combining Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) based on the envelope entropy selection criterion for rolling bearing fault diagnosis. First, the VMD method is used to decompose the vibration signal into several Intrinsic Mode Function (IMF) components, and the envelope spectrum of these components is obtained through envelope analysis. Then, the envelope entropy is adopted as the IMF component selection criterion to select the IMF components that best reflect the fault characteristics. The envelope energy of the selected IMF components is used as feature indicators and input into the SVM model to achieve fault type recognition. This method is applied to the fault diagnosis experiment of rolling bearing vibration signals, and the results show that the method can accurately extract fault features and effectively recognize fault types. The experimental results indicate that the fault recognition accuracy of this method reaches 99.5%. By comparing with other methods, the superiority and practical application value of this method in rolling bearing fault diagnosis are verified.

articleTitle: Research on portable testing technology for smart combine terminals
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: For a long period, the power system has traditionally been made up of components such as power generation, transmission, transformation, distribution, and consumption. With the advancement of information technology, the relationship between the distribution and consumption sectors has become increasingly intertwined. Many countries, in accordance with their own developmental needs, have proposed plans for the integration of distribution and consumption. In China, the smart combine terminal has been developed as the core equipment for the integration of distribution and consumption. It has complex functions and high reliability requirements, and currently, there is a lack of effective testing methods to detect its complex functions, such as power grid operation monitoring and topological analysis. This paper introduces a portable testing technology for the smart combine terminal of district areas. Firstly, it constructs a knowledge base of district working conditions to simulate the operating state of the district. Secondly, it designs the software and hardware architecture of the testing system, and finally, it tests the testing device. The experimental results show that this portable testing device is capable of conducting a comprehensive inspection of the smart combine terminal, including advanced business functions, in both distribution and consumption aspects.

articleTitle: A 2-channel TIADC frequency response mismatch calibration method based on frequency domain adaptive filtering
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: To achieve high sample rates, the system can utilize multiple analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) employing the time-interleaved analog-to-digital conversion (TIADC) technique. In TIADC, the calibration of mismatch error has received much attention. In this brief, a calibration method for frequency response mismatch (FRM) of two-channel time-interleaved analogue-to-digital converters (TIADCs) is proposed. The channel frequency response is approximated by means of polynomial fitting and the coefficients of the polynomials are estimated using a frequency domain adaptive filtering (FDAF) algorithm. The desire signal of adaptive filter can be exploit with slight oversampling. Utilizing the acquired coefficients, it is possible to compensate for the FRM of the parallel acquisition system. The proposed algorithm provides more accurate gradient estimation and faster rate of convergence compared to the traditional algorithm. We construct a dual-channel TIADC system with a sampling rate of 12.5 GSPS. The simulation result also shows the efficiency of the proposed calibration method. After applying the proposed calibration algorithm, SNR of the system is improved about 22 dB.

articleTitle: The image perspective correction methods for Parkinson's scale actions assessment
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Parkinson's Disease is a neurodegenerative disorder commonly classified as a movement disorder. The symptoms of Parkinson's can be assessed through various types of testing methods. Compared to Parkinson's assessment methods based on various human body sensors, computer vision-based assessment methods are more convenient and efficient. In a home environment, however, the camera cannot always maintain a standard posture, which often leads to poor image quality. Therefore, this paper proposes an image correction method based on human body bounding boxes. The corrective effect of the method on the patient's scale movements from various perspectives was tested by comparing it with benchmark data from the Vicon system. The average pixel error has been reduced from over 80 to below 10, and the correction effectiveness rate is now over 80%. This method enables the assessment of Parkinson's symptoms to be conducted at home using only a smartphone. It offers robust support for non-invasive, real-time assessment of Parkinson's symptoms, providing potential convenience for daily care and remote monitoring of Parkinson's patients.

articleTitle: Optimization algorithm for communication energy consumption of energy meters in power load management system
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The new power load management system, as a modern power monitoring system in the context of rapid development of science and technology, can effectively enhance the communication function and detection performance of the system by leveraging Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). The primary challenge is effectively regulating power grid energy usage for sustained and reliable performance. The paper proposes an optimization algorithm, EB-NSGA-II-LEACH, to address the issue of energy imbalance in the traditional S-LEACH algorithm. This improved approach incorporates both energy balance and NSGA-II algorithm. By adjusting the cluster head's node selection probability, it achieves balanced energy consumption and mitigates excessive energy depletion in certain nodes. Simultaneously, the NSGA-II algorithm is employed to address multiple objective functions and identify a range of non-dominated solutions as the optimal approach to enhance network lifespan and attain energy consumption equilibrium.

articleTitle: Research status and dynamic analysis of damping and vibration reduction technology of rotating machinery rotor system
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Large rotating machinery in nuclear, power, and petrochemical industries employ multi-span flexible connections. As the rotor length-to-diameter ratio rises, rigid rotors become flexible, exceeding critical speeds and inducing resonance. This challenges supercritical technologies like damping, vibration reduction, balancing, and driving. In view of the vibration problems of flexible rotor systems with wide-band, multi-mode, and multi-criticality, this paper examines damping and vibration reduction. It highlights modern industrial rotating machinery's evolution, analyzes gyro effects, and critiques traditional damping designs like squeeze film dampers for their limited application range. The paper then delves into rotor vibration control, categorizing technologies as active or passive, and outlining principles, advantages, and disadvantages. Active technology offers precision but high costs; passive technology is cost-effective yet limited in effect and scope. Finally, the research and application status of damping and vibration reduction technology in aerospace, civil engineering, machinery, transportation, and other fields are analyzed, which provides a theoretical reference for vibration reduction and noise reduction technology of rotating machinery.

articleTitle: Multi-robot path planning and cooperative obstacle avoidance based on Monte-Carlo tree search
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technologies, multi-robot cooperative processing tasks are becoming more and more common in various applications. However, traditional single-robot planning algorithms show obvious limitations in dealing with complex social interactions and dynamic environments in the real world. To address this challenge, this paper applies Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to multi-robot path planning and proposes a collaborative obstacle avoidance motion planning algorithm based on MCTS. Specifically, the algorithm prunes the Monte Carlo tree by excluding cases that do not meet the robot speed constraints and potential collisions, which significantly improves the computational speed and success rate of the algorithm, making it applicable to the multi-robot path conflict problem. In addition, we design a policy space that conforms to the robot's operation and a cost function that meets the requirements of robot path planning to plan an efficient cooperative path for each robot. Through a series of simulation experiments, we demonstrate the algorithm's path planning and obstacle avoidance performance in a variety of conflict scenarios. The results show that the method is highly cooperative and effective in complex environments.

articleTitle: Effective task scheduling for intelligent manufacturing with fog computing
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Effective task scheduling is crucial for the real-time processing of manufacturing tasks, particularly in the context of intelligent manufacturing within a fog computing environment. The paper introduces a novel task scheduling strategy known as the Level Mapping Task Scheduling (LMTS). This strategy is specifically designed to address the challenges posed by complex task requirements and the heterogeneity of fog nodes. The LMTS leverages a level mapping mechanism to ensure an optimal match between tasks and fog nodes, effectively reducing both the scope of task scheduling and the algorithm's complexity. This mechanism is pivotal in achieving a balance between task real-time performance and resource utilization efficiency. In the proposed strategy, virtualization technology is employed to manage the computing resources of the fog servers. This allows for a more flexible and efficient allocation of resources, which is essential for handling the diverse and dynamic nature of manufacturing tasks. Each mapping branch is encapsulated within a container, enabling the solution to be completed in an isolated and secure environment. The LMTS strategy significantly enhances the real-time performance of tasks by minimizing service delays, which is a critical factor in manufacturing processes. Moreover, it is evaluated and compared with the existing scheduling strategies through simulation experiment, the results show that the proposed strategy can reduce service delay of task.

articleTitle: Failed elements correction method based on multi-strategy grey wolf optimizer
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Addressing the issues of the classical Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) algorithm, such as the simplicity of its search strategy and limited application scope, this paper proposes a Multi-strategy Grey Wolf Optimizer (MGWO) algorithm based on a combination of nonlinear bi-convergence factor strategy and Gaussian mutation. Furthermore, the algorithm is integrated with the improved discovery mechanism of the Cuckoo Search algorithm and the Logistic-Sine-Cosine chaotic mapping, which is applied to array synthesis under the condition of array element failure. The objective function incorporates additional common excitation constraints to reduce the maintenance cost of the antenna system and enhance its stability. Compared to the existing strategy, the number of corrections of the whole excitations of the working elements is reduced by up to 33%. Furthermore, the radiation characteristics of the recovered pattern satisfy the specified requirements, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on the recognition of welding defects by modified ViT model combined with Canny algorithm
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: An improved Vision Transformer (ViT) model incorporating the Canny algorithm is proposed to address the low accuracy and efficiency issues in manually interpreting radiographic images for weld defect detection. The aim is to assist in recognizing typical welding defects and thereby enhance the accuracy and efficiency of interpretation. To enhance the model's capability in capturing local information, an edge feature extraction module based on the Canny algorithm is incorporated into the original ViT architecture, leveraging the advantage of global perception in ViT while addressing its limitations in handling local texture features. By parallelizing the edge extraction module with the ViT main architecture and fusing features at appropriate positions, the processing of global and local information is effectively balanced, leading to improved model generalization. Transfer learning is employed to reduce the model's data requirements during training, addressing the challenge of acquiring large-scale, high-quality weld radiographic datasets. The research findings demonstrate that the proposed model achieves significant performance improvements in weld defect recognition, achieving recognition accuracies of 98.97% and 95.94% on self-built datasets and the RIAWELC dataset, respectively. Compared to the original ViT model, these results represent an increase of 2.24% and 0.27%, respectively. Additionally, when compared with other mainstream image recognition models, enhancements ranging from 0.74% to 4.12% are observed with the proposed model, thus meeting the practical demand for interpreting weld radiographic images in production scenarios.

articleTitle: Research progress on wireless sensor networks for mechanical vibration monitoring: a CiteSpace visualization analysis approach
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: The application of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) in mechanical vibration monitoring is pivotal for achieving efficient monitoring within the realms of industrial automation and intelligent manufacturing, playing a significant role in the digital transformation and upgrading of China's manufacturing industry. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the major technological advancements made by scholars and institutions globally over the past sixteen years in the domain of mechanical vibration monitoring using WSNs. Subsequently, employing CiteSpace for knowledge mapping and visualization, a multifaceted statistical analysis is conducted on over four hundred publications from both domestic and international sources. Through clustering analysis, keyword co-occurrence, and other analytical techniques, the paper delineates the multidimensional evolution of research hotspots and the dynamics of author collaboration networks over time. Building on this foundation, the paper delves into the cutting-edge trends of the field, emphasizing the critical importance of establishing efficient energy management systems and leveraging machine learning and artificial intelligence to process large-scale sensor data. These strategies are essential for optimizing system performance and propelling the development of WSNs towards miniaturization, integration, multifunctionality, systematization, and networking. The synergistic effects of these measures are anticipated to provide robust support for the intelligent upgrade of the manufacturing industry, fostering its progression towards greater efficiency and intelligence.

articleTitle: Comprehensive transmission sequence anomaly detection based on RFE-PAA and BI-LSTM-CNN
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of industrial technology, the structure of transmission systems has become increasingly complex, posing more severe challenges to their real-time monitoring and anomaly detection systems. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel comprehensive transmission sequence anomaly detection method. Firstly, the method employs Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) to select the most relevant temporal features for precise identification of the anomaly detection target variables. Subsequently, Piecewise Aggregate Approximation (PAA) is utilized for effective dimensionality reduction of the time series data to simplify the subsequent processing steps. Finally, by integrating Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), a deep anomaly detection model is constructed to identify abnormal states efficiently. An example analysis of time series anomaly detection in transmission system oil leakage demonstrates the significant advantages of this method in improving the accuracy and efficiency of anomaly detection. The results indicate that this method can provide a new, reliable, and efficient technical solution for anomaly detection in complex transmission systems.

articleTitle: A real-time cardiac electrical model on FPGA for closed-loop test of CIED
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: Abnormalities in the cardiac electrical activity can be treated with cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED). Problems that occur in the closed-loop interaction between CIED and heart are difficult to detect through only open-loop testing. For the closed-loop interaction between CIED and heart model, this paper presents a frontal two-dimensional real-time heart model composed of 14861 units and 28044 paths. The model achieves a balance between computational complexity and expressive ability. The generation and conduction of excitation is simulated with Aliev-Panfilov phenomenological action potential model. With the electrophysiology, the generation of electrocardiogram (ECG) and electrogram (EGM) is based on the action potential of units. Finally, implemented on FPGA hardware platform through units grouping and pipeline technology, the heart model can generate EGM, ECG signals and conduction state snapshots in real time and respond to real-time stimulation input. The hardware framework of the heart model is scalable. The completed real-time heart model can simulate the origin of cardiac excitation and the conduction of electrical activity under normal sinus rhythm, block and premature beat conditions, which meets the real-time requirements of CIED closed-loop testing. The ECG generation process in the model can be explained with conduction state snapshots and electrophysiology.

articleTitle: Review of research on occlusion issues in RGB-D dynamic scene 3D reconstruction
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: As innovation proceeds to advance, 3D recreation innovation has ended up a critical portion of the field of computer vision. Among these, 3D reproduction innovation based on RGB-D information sources has ended up a well known approach in later a long time. Right now, the more develop inactive 3D recreation calculations have ended up progressively successful for reproducing stationary objects. Be that as it may, their adequacy lessens when parts of the scene are blocked. This paper briefly presents particular approaches to address impediment issues and the fundamental concepts of energetic 3D remaking innovation based on RGB-D information sources. The points of interest and current investigate status of energetic 3D reproduction focusing on impediment issues utilizing RGB-D information sources are examined. Moreover, the most recent progressions in 3D remaking of energetic scenes are summarized, and proposed future investigate bearings.

articleTitle: Application of data factors in healthcare industry
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In the era of digital economy, data has become a key factor of production, playing a crucial role in economic growth, social progress and innovative activities. The governance of data factors is a foundational support for modernizing national governance in the digital age.In healthcare industry, the sources of data are quite extensive, including patients' information, medical institutions' diagnostic and treatment materials, and public health data from the government and health organizations. These data often contain sensitive personal information and identity identification information, making issues of personal privacy and data security particularly important.To address issues of data supply and demand, trading, circulation, and application in healthcare industry, based on the characteristics of data, this paper analyzes the difficulties of data factorization and the requirements for data factorization in healthcare industry, introduces the idea of "intermediate state" of data, and constructs architectures such as privacy computing and blockchain to solve privacy and security issues in the process of data factor usage and circulation. This solution can be applied in healthcare industry to provide relevant feasibility plans for the security and privacy protection of medical data, support the application and circulation of medical data factors, and effectively promote the development of data factors in healthcare industry.

articleTitle: Dense point cloud map construction based on ORB-SLAM2 and cross-attention network
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Test Automation & Instrumentation (ISTAI 2024)
abstract: In the field of 3D vision technology, binocular vision technology, as a representative of low-cost and high-efficiency methods, has gained widespread attention and holds superior application prospects in the industrial sector. The current state-of-the-art binocular sparse visual SLAM systems can accurately and reliably estimate camera trajectories and landmark positions. However, these sparse maps are solely used for localization and cannot be employed for other tasks such as obstacle avoidance or scene understanding. To address this, this paper proposes a framework for constructing dense point cloud maps in binocular sparse visual SLAM systems. This framework enhances the traditional ORB-SLAM2 algorithm by incorporating depth estimation using a cross-attention network to complete depth information and build dense point cloud maps based on its localization capabilities. For the first-frame image, the proportion of incorrectly predicted pixels in the KITTI dataset is only 1.77%. The proposed method is effective and robust on common datasets, suitable for constructing dense point cloud maps in outdoor large-scale scenes. The output model is overall comprehensive and detailed, holding significant practical value in various outdoor scenarios.
